options.option: More profiles, coefficients, contact values or linear internal branches
options.apparatus_and_reference: The present linear rod framework already specifies these changes, but the same entropy derivative, common-stress elimination and independent entropy-coordinate solver apply.
options.calibration: A chosen symmetry or chi0 subset can still make the two models agree exactly. Exact calibration degeneracy alone would not make this a new physical question.

minimum_complete_apparatus: Explicitly replace the current first-order thermodynamic scope by an exact caloric material over a declared positive-temperature and small-strain domain. Retain specified reference-volume mechanics and conduction, or specify the geometric terms if that approximation is relaxed.

A possible exact small-strain thermal free-energy term is ce*[T-T0-T*log(T/T0)], with the same linear thermal-strain coupling. It gives ce*log(T/T0) entropy and constant fixed-strain heat capacity; this is an illustrative new constitutive choice, not the existing task at larger amplitude.

Specify heaters, held preparation, clamp work, thermal-body/contact energy, time origin and the ordinary temperature or calorimetric readout. Internal-variable production heats the stated local thermal subsystem; it is not stored spring energy.
options.derived_balance_for_that_illustrative_ch: With B=(beta0+beta1)*epsilon-beta1*z and eta*z_dot=-psi_z, the first law gives ce*T_dot+T*B_dot=div(k*grad T)+eta*z_dot^2 in the geometrically linear reference-volume model. The source could retain the correct nonlinear reversible coupling but extend the no-internal-heating approximation beyond its first-order range.
options.exact_shared_calibration: For an explicitly defined amplitude-scaled preparation, the derivative of each response at zero amplitude is shared because eta*z_dot^2 is second order. Nonzero finite-frequency or transient linear-response measurements can identify conductivity. Finite-amplitude raw calibration readings are not exactly shared merely because their heating is small.
options.identification_qualification: The linearized equations can reuse the r4 calibration mechanism, but a new measurement protocol and its complete-domain identification/noise checks must be fixed independently. The existing r4 sampled identification is not an analytic theorem for an arbitrary new calibration.
options.independent_reference_needed: A conservative internal-energy finite-volume evolution and separately derived entropy/internal-strain evolution, with common-stress constraints, preparation work and spatial/time refinement. Neither has been implemented or timed for this nonlinear option.
blockers: The omitted production is an explicit positive dissipation term; the r4 passer already derives the thermodynamic balance and tests its energy conservation. No evidence establishes this as harder physics.

A simple switch from spring work to heat repeats the Maxwell-contact storage/heat distinction already packaged in hydrodynamic-heating r3; this outline should instead be assessed on actual bulk nonlinear temperature evolution.

No finite amplitude range, robust signal above the unchanged .025 K gate, nonlinear stability/temperature positivity, fixed instrument-noise study or verifier runtime has been established. Increasing amplitude or dividing by amplitude squared solely to magnify a weak error is not validated here.

options.apparatus_and_reference: A finite heater/clamp history and the moment of release would determine z by the same constitutive dynamics. A direct evolution through preparation, then release, would be an independent check of any preparation map.
options.calibration: Infinite-wait preparations give exact shared relaxed states; finite waits generally do not. A new exact subset must retain identifiable conductivity and meaningful nonzero measurements.
options.blocker: Replacing the prescribed finite-history state by relaxed z would merely discard a stated initial-state control. Retaining exact preparation and changing only caloric elimination repeats r4. The current pass already constructs the correct held-relaxed state; no substantive alternative assumption and robust margin have been demonstrated.

bounded_overlap_read.relevance: Exact Maxwell contact mechanics, cycle-mean calibration and phase-resolved dashpot heat versus spring work already test stored-energy/heat attribution.
Already uses an exact first-order calibration with a second-order constrained mechanical readout. It is not the same rod physics; it prevents describing the perturbative-order pattern itself as new.

Already tests finite-time calorimeter heat against exact mechanical work with intervening stored energy. Adding finite-time storage calorimetry to the rod would need a different unresolved assumption.
